title: Spice + Mortar
intro: A modular spice storage system, designed as my graduation project. Small details, big changes.
brief: Spices travel halfway around the world to reach our kitchens, then end up in storage full of small, everyday irritations. The aim was a system that removes them quietly: easy to reach and use with one hand, compact on the wall, and flexible enough to suit any kitchen and any cook.
did: Through rounds of prototyping and user testing, the spice unit became a slim container that works with one hand and guides itself back into place. For crushing, I chose a mortar over a mill, so a single module works for every spice and keeps the cook involved in the process.

The system follows what I call limited customisation: enough choice to fit any kitchen, not so much that it overwhelms the buyer or complicates production. Set-ups are built in a four-step online configurator, and every one gets a code that can be shared or reordered.

images.alt: Five prototype versions of the spice container
images.text: I have tested over 10 versions of containers and lids, and the testers chose the sliding lid unanimously, and the shaker opening closes itself as the lid opens.

images.title: Packaging & branding
images.text: Nothing printed, everything embossed. The gilded part of the logo shows what's inside, and every box opens the same way: push, and it slides out.
